summary: All 9 applicable online boxes (.110 .123 .124 .133 .171 .184 .186 .240 .243) were verified again in ONE Unreal Gold 226 deathmatch on the host server 192.168.1.132:7807 (DmDeck16): the GameSpy roster names all nine Fleet<octet> players, server.log has an IP line and 'Join succeeded' for each with no disconnect, and every fresh frame shows the shared scoreboard. .143 is NA (Unreal.exe bugchecks nv4_disp). The game was closed on all 9 boxes and PROCLIST confirms it. .243's User.ini was put back to its original (md5 b532260a..., read back).
issues: .133 (whole round) and .184 (later in the round) sent almost no client traffic to :7807: 3-5 and 10-14 packets per 8-12 s, against 250-1500 from the others. The server kept sending to them at about 20/s and kept both on the roster with pings, and their frames advanced. They were connected and receiving, but their uplink rate is unexplained: low client tick/fps, or input not being sent. Check it on each box (client framerate, NetSpeed, Unreal.log) before relying on them for real play.
UICLICK (Fire) did not respawn a dead player on any box tested (.110, .133, .184), so click-based input could not be used to tell a healthy uplink from a weak one.

kill: unreal.exe had to be FORCED on .110 .124 .133 .171 .240 (WM_CLOSE was ignored for 12 s). It closed gracefully on .123 .184 .186. .243 was quit via its console and then PROCKILL. Desktop modes after the forced kills were not re-read; the next round should confirm that .124 (vcr-kmd) and .243 (Voodoo 2) are back at their desktop.
.186 still has an orphaned 'Windows Security Alert' firewall dialog from the launch.

XP boxes and .186 keep the round's User.ini edits (Name=Fleet<octet>, NetSpeed 20000, F9=open 192.168.1.132:7807). They are harmless but differ from the library, and the next GAMESYNC may overwrite them.
